name: Team Workflow Audit
description: Iteration 2: compliance branch, meeting load question, tool_count dropped for variant B, expandable recommendation.

experiment.description: A: full questionnaire, neutral copy. B: work-mode first, benefit-led copy, no tool_count question, 30-day plan CTA.

intro.title: Get your team's 30-day workflow plan
intro.body: Answer a few quick questions and we'll build a plan tailored to how your team actually works. Takes about a minute.

work_mode.subtitle: This shapes the whole plan, so we ask it first.

priorities.subtitle: Pick up to three. We'll weight recommendations accordingly.

meeting_hours.title: How many hours a week does a typical teammate spend in meetings?
meeting_hours.hint: Your plan will include concrete ways to win some of them back.

results.title: Regulated team at scale
results.body: A team of your size with compliance as a priority needs a workflow that produces audit evidence automatically — not one that relies on people remembering to document.
highlights: Route every change through a tracked approval in the task tracker
Centralise identity: SSO for all tools, quarterly access reviews
Generate change logs and release notes from version control
details: You selected compliance among your priorities and your team has 20+ people, so the biggest risk is inconsistent evidence across sub-teams.
Teams at this size usually pass audits faster when approvals and logs are by-products of the normal workflow rather than a separate process.
Start with the tools that touch customer data; expand SSO/SCIM coverage from there.

results.title: Meeting-heavy team
results.body: Your teammates spend a large part of the week in meetings. The fastest win is moving status and decisions to written, async formats.
highlights: Replace recurring status meetings with written weekly updates
Introduce two no-meeting focus blocks per week
Give every meeting a written decision log
details: You reported 15+ meeting hours per teammate per week — above the range where teams usually report sustained focus time.
Async written updates typically reclaim 3–5 hours per person per week in the first month.
Keep synchronous time for decisions that need debate; move everything else to documents.

results.title: Remote team, too many tools
results.body: Your team is fully remote and juggles a lot of tools. Context switching is probably your biggest hidden cost.
highlights: Consolidate chat, docs and tasks into at most three tools
Introduce a written weekly plan instead of status meetings
Set a single source of truth for decisions
details: You are fully remote and reported 8+ daily tools; remote teams feel tool sprawl most because every hand-off happens inside a tool.
Consolidation usually pays back within a quarter in reduced onboarding time alone.

results.title: Remote-first, async-ready
results.body: A fully remote team with a lean toolset. Your leverage is in async rituals and written communication.
highlights: Move status updates to written async check-ins
Define response-time expectations per channel
Record decisions in one searchable place
details: You are fully remote with a manageable toolset, so the next step is making communication norms explicit.
Written response-time expectations remove most of the ‘always on’ pressure in remote teams.

results.title: Office-first team
results.body: Your team spends most of the week together. Protect focus time and make the in-office days count.
highlights: Cluster meetings into two office days
Introduce no-meeting focus blocks
Keep a written record for the days people are out
details: You reported 4+ office days; co-located teams lose focus time to ad-hoc interruptions rather than to meetings.
Clustering synchronous work into fixed days protects the remaining ones.

results.title: Compliance-driven workflow
results.body: Audit readiness is one of your priorities. Your workflow should produce evidence as a by-product of normal work.
highlights: Make approvals explicit in the task tracker
Automate change logs from version control
Review access rights quarterly
details: You selected compliance among your priorities; for a team of your size a lightweight approval trail is enough.
Pick one system of record for approvals before adding any new tooling.

results.title: Balanced hybrid team
results.body: No single bottleneck stands out. Small, consistent improvements to rituals will give you the most return.
highlights: Agree on which days are for collaboration and which for focus
Run a monthly tooling review
Keep decisions written and searchable
details: None of the stronger signals (remote + many tools, heavy meetings, compliance at scale) applied to your answers.
Teams in this position get the most from fixing one ritual at a time and measuring the effect.
